citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) as in
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]];
it supplies the stated Hilbert-space construction and is not a physical
measurement assumption. Fix one finite nonempty label set $J$ with
$N:=|J|\ge1$, an enumeration of
$J$ by $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and dimensionless real coordinates
$q=(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in\mathbb R^N$. The labels may represent sites of a
fixed finite spatial lattice or a fixed finite set of modes; any graph,
geometry, and couplings are additional fixed regulator data. The coordinate
space, Hilbert space, and polynomial differential expression are those of
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]]:
$H_N=L^2(\mathbb R^N,dq;\mathbb C)$, with inner product linear in its first
variable, $D_0=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb C)$, and

$$h_0u=-\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\partial_j^2u+V(q)u,\qquad u\in D_0,$$

where $a_j>0$ and $V$ is a real polynomial. Require fixed constants $c>0$ and
$C_0\ge0$ such that

$$V(q)\ge c|q|^2-C_0\qquad(q\in\mathbb R^N).$$

For this physical model, take $q_j$, $a_j$, $c$, $C_0$, and the coefficients
of $V$ to be dimensionless. Adopt a positive energy scale $E_*$ in joules as
primitive finite-regulator data, and use $\hbar$ in joule-seconds under
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. When the mathematical supplier
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]] constructs its specified
self-adjoint form realization $h$ of $h_0$, the model Hamiltonian is
$H_{\rm phys}:=E_*h$ on that supplied domain. This postulate adopts the
finite-regulator polynomial data; it does not assert that the initial
differential expression is self-adjoint or choose an operator domain by
itself.

The finite label set and polynomial are held fixed. A finite spatial regulator
is not thereby Lorentz invariant, and this model asserts no continuum or
infinite-volume limit, no convergence of a perturbation series, and no
reported observation. Its parameters are selected model inputs, not measured
values.

Adopt the following physical reading only for an explicitly selected model
whose mathematical data have actually been constructed. Let $\mathscr H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $\rho_t$ be the model's density operator at
a time $t$ at which a measurement is made, and let
$\{M_{a,r}:r=1,\ldots,q_a\}_{a=1}^m$ be a supplied normalized finite bounded
Kraus instrument on $\mathscr H$ in the exact sense of
[[def-qft-finite-bounded-kraus-instrument]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ when using the normalization result of
[[lem-qft-finite-instrument-normalization]]. Its hypotheses include that
$\rho_t$ is a density operator and that the instrument really satisfies
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}=I_{\mathscr H}$; the supplier's result is a draft
with a complete conditional proof, not an independent approval or an
apparatus-realization theorem.

Put

$$E_a:=\sum_rM_{a,r}^*M_{a,r},\qquad
\mathcal J_a(X):=\sum_rM_{a,r}XM_{a,r}^*.$$

As the **Born interpretation postulate** for this selected model, read

$$p_a(t):=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal J_a(\rho_t))
=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_tE_a)$$

as the model probability for outcome $a$. The mathematical supplier proves
$p_a(t)\in[0,1]$ and $\sum_{a=1}^mp_a(t)=1$ under the hypotheses just
listed. When $p_a(t)>0$, adopt
$\mathcal J_a(\rho_t)/p_a(t)$ as the model's conditional state after outcome
$a$; at zero probability no normalized update is assigned. These are
model-level probability assignments, not observations.

If the selected construction supplies a self-adjoint observable in the sense
of [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]] and its
spectral projection-valued measure as in
[[def-projection-valued-measure]], a declared finite Borel partition may be
used only after its projections have been constructed and verified as a
finite projective instrument. In that case the projections are the single
Kraus operators for their outcomes. A supplied bounded effect is read as an
outcome effect only as part of a supplied normalized instrument; this item
does not construct square roots, a spectral measure, or an instrument from an
arbitrary formal observable.

If a model has actually constructed a self-adjoint Hamiltonian $\widehat H$
and its unitary evolution, adopt the Schrödinger convention
$U(t)=\exp(-it\widehat H/\hbar)$ and
$\rho_t=U(t)\rho_0U(t)^*$ when that construction establishes that $\rho_t$
is a density operator. In the Heisenberg representation use
$O_H(t)=U(t)^*O\,U(t)$. This postulate neither constructs the Hamiltonian,
unitary group, state, field representation, nor their domains.

The model declaration identifies the selected species, field normalization,
regulator, preparation and measurement data using
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. It does not assert that every classical action
has a quantization, that every formal state is positive, or that any cutoff
can be removed. In particular it supplies no interacting continuum
four-dimensional QED Hilbert space, scattering operator, asymptotic
completeness, LSZ limit, or nonperturbative convergence. A formal coefficient
is not an exact probability without an additional controlled approximation
map and a constructed model. Agreement with reported data would test the
selected approximation and empirical inputs; it would not prove this
postulate or the model. No reported data are asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice and the data of
[[lem-qft-polynomial-positive-compact-resolvent]]. Its variational operator $R$
is compact, self-adjoint, positive, and injective on the infinite-dimensional
complex Hilbert space $H_N$. Let $(\mu_n)_{n\ge1}$ be its positive eigenvalues
in nonincreasing order, with multiplicity, and choose corresponding
orthonormal eigenvectors $(\psi_n)_{n\ge1}$. Put
$E_n:=\mu_n^{-1}-1$ and define
$$D(S):=\left\{u=\sum_{n\ge1}c_n\psi_n\in H_N:\sum_{n\ge1}E_n^2|c_n|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad Su:=\sum_{n\ge1}E_nc_n\psi_n.$$
The series for $u$ converges in $H_N$ by the Hilbert-space expansion theorem.
Then $S$ is self-adjoint and satisfies $\langle Su,u\rangle\ge\|u\|_2^2$
for every $u\in D(S)$; also $(S+I)^{-1}=R$ is compact. For every
$u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb C)$,
$$Su=-\sum_{j=1}^Na_j\partial_j^2u+Wu.$$
Consequently $h:=S-(C_0+1)I$, on the same domain, is a self-adjoint realization
of the differential expression in
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]] and satisfies
$\langle hu,u\rangle\ge-C_0\|u\|_2^2$ for every $u\in D(h)$.
It has compact resolvent, meaning that for some $z\in\mathbb C$ the map
$h-zI:D(h)\to H_N$ is bijective with bounded inverse on $H_N$, and that
inverse is compact; here $z=-(C_0+2)$ and $(h+(C_0+2)I)^{-1}=R$. Put
$\lambda_n:=E_n-C_0-1$, the eigenvalues of $h$; equivalently,
$$D(h)=\left\{u=\sum_nc_n\psi_n:\sum_n\lambda_n^2|c_n|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
For every $u\in Q$,
$$a(u,u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(E_n+1)|\langle u,\psi_n\rangle|^2,\qquad q_h(u):=a(u,u)-(C_0+2)\|u\|_2^2 =\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n|\langle u,\psi_n\rangle|^2.$$
The lowest eigenvalue is attained and has finite multiplicity. This selects a
form realization; it does not assert that the differential expression on
$C_c^\infty$ is essentially self-adjoint or that it has no other self-adjoint
extensions.

Assume Countable Choice and let $h$ be the self-adjoint operator of
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]], with complete orthonormal
eigenfamily $(\psi_n)_{n\ge1}$ and real eigenvalues
$\lambda_n=E_n-C_0-1$. For $t\in\mathbb R$ define
$$U(t)f:=\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-it\lambda_n}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n \qquad(f\in H_N).$$
Then the series converges in $H_N$ for every $f$; $U(t)$ is unitary,
$U(0)=I$, $U(s+t)=U(s)U(t)$, and $t\mapsto U(t)f$ is norm-continuous for
every $f$. Its norm derivative at any $t$ exists exactly for $f\in D(h)$, and
then
$$\frac{d}{dt}U(t)f=-i\,hU(t)f.$$
This is a mathematical one-parameter group with a dimensionless real
parameter; it makes no physical unit or empirical claim.

derivations.claim:
Under Countable Choice [A1], the hypotheses of [F1] hold, so $h$ is
self-adjoint on $D(h)$. Multiplication by the positive
real scalar $E_*$ preserves self-adjointness and the domain, so
$H_{\rm phys}=E_*h$ is self-adjoint on $D(h)$ with eigenvalues
$E_*\lambda_n$. The units in [A2] make $E_*\tau/\hbar$ dimensionless.

Put $s=E_*\tau/\hbar$. Since this is a real linear change of parameter,
Countable Choice [A1] discharges the hypothesis of [F2], which gives
unitarity, strong continuity, the identity at zero, and the group
law for $U_{\rm phys}(\tau)=U(s)$. Unitarity also gives
$\|U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi\|=\|\psi\|$.

If $\psi\in D(h)$, the chain rule and [F2] give
$\frac{d}{d\tau}U(E_*\tau/\hbar)\psi
=-i(E_*/\hbar)hU(E_*\tau/\hbar)\psi
=-iH_{\rm phys}U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi/\hbar$.
Conversely, because $E_*/\hbar>0$, the change $s=E_*\tau/\hbar$ is
invertible, so norm differentiability in $\tau$ is equivalent to
differentiability in $s$; [F2] makes its domain exactly $D(h)$.

[A3] supplies the physical reading of this already constructed
self-adjoint Hamiltonian and group as the selected model's Schrödinger
evolution. It adds no existence claim beyond [F1] and [F2], and no empirical
premise is used.

By [F2], $\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}>0$ is dimensionless.
The eigenvalues of $H_{\rm phys}=E_*h$ are $E_*\lambda_k$, so its Gibbs
weights are
$e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}E_*\lambda_k}
=e^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}$. Therefore
$Z_T=\sum_ke^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}$.

Under Countable Choice [A1], apply [F1] at $\widehat\beta>0$. It gives
$Z_T>0$, the stated finite
upper bound, and trace-class positivity of $e^{-\widehat\beta h}$.
Dividing by $Z_T$ yields $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_T)=1$ and preserves
positivity and trace class.

Under the same Countable Choice assumption [A1], for bounded $B$, [F1]
gives the absolutely convergent sum for
$\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\widehat\beta h}B)$. Since
$\rho_T=Z_T^{-1}e^{-\widehat\beta h}$, linearity of the trace and
$Z_T>0$ give the displayed normalized formula. If $B=E_a$ is an effect in
the instrument of [A3], that postulate supplies its physical model
probability interpretation; the finite trace calculation supplies its
value.

and its unitary evolution, adopt the Schrödinger convention
$U(t)=\exp(-it\widehat H/\hbar)$ and
$\rho_t=U(t)\rho_0U(t)^*$ when that construction establishes that $\rho_t$
is a density operator. In the Heisenberg representation use
$O_H(t)=U(t)^*O\,U(t)$. This postulate neither constructs the Hamiltonian,
unitary group, state, field representation, nor their domains.

The model declaration identifies the selected species, field normalization,
regulator, preparation and measurement data using
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. It does not assert that every classical action
has a quantization, that every formal state is positive, or that any cutoff
can be removed. In particular it supplies no interacting continuum
four-dimensional QED Hilbert space, scattering operator, asymptotic
completeness, LSZ limit, or nonperturbative convergence. A formal coefficient
is not an exact probability without an additional controlled approximation
map and a constructed model. Agreement with reported data would test the
selected approximation and empirical inputs; it would not prove this
postulate or the model. No reported data are asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice. Use the finite data and notation of
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]]: $N\ge1$,
$H_N=L^2(\mathbb R^N,dq;\mathbb C)$, $D_0=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb C)$,
and $W=V+C_0+1\ge1+c|q|^2$. For $u,v\in D_0$ define
$$a(u,v):=\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\int_{\mathbb R^N}(\partial_j u)\overline{\partial_jv}\,dq+\int_{\mathbb R^N}(W+1)u\overline v\,dq,$$
and $\|u\|_Q:=a(u,u)^{1/2}$. Let $Q$ be the completion of this inner-product
space, constructed as equivalence classes of $\|\cdot\|_Q$-Cauchy sequences.
Then $Q$ is a complex Hilbert space and the map sending a Cauchy class to its
$L^2$ limit is a continuous injective linear map $Q\hookrightarrow H_N$ with
dense image. Each $u\in Q$ has weak derivatives $\partial_j u\in L^2$ and a
weighted function $\sqrt{W+1}\,u\in L^2$, and
$$\|u\|_Q^2=\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\|\partial_j u\|_2^2+\|\sqrt{W+1}\,u\|_2^2.$$
Here $g_j=\partial_j u$ means explicitly that
$\int u\,\overline{\partial_j\varphi}=-\int g_j\overline\varphi$ for every
$\varphi\in D_0$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $N\ge1$, $a_1,\ldots,a_N>0$ and $c>0$. Let
$Q_{\mathrm{osc}}$ be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb C)$
for the form inner product
$$a_{\mathrm{osc}}(u,v):=\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\int (\partial_j u)\overline{\partial_jv} +\int (c|q|^2+2)u\overline v.$$
This is the space $Q$ of
[[lem-qft-coercive-polynomial-form-domain]] for $V(q)=c|q|^2$ and $C_0=0$.
For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_N)\in\mathbb N_0^N$, there is a smooth product
Hermite function $\psi_{\mathbf n}$ such that
$$\langle\psi_{\mathbf n},\psi_{\mathbf m}\rangle_{L^2}=\delta_{\mathbf n\mathbf m},\qquad \overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\psi_{\mathbf n}\}=L^2(\mathbb R^N),$$
and
$$\left(-\sum_{j=1}^Na_j\partial_j^2+c|q|^2\right)\psi_{\mathbf n} =\epsilon_{\mathbf n}\psi_{\mathbf n},\qquad \epsilon_{\mathbf n}:=\sum_{j=1}^N(2n_j+1)\sqrt{a_jc}.$$
For the ground multi-index $\mathbf0$, the smooth representative is
$$\psi_{\mathbf0}(q)=\prod_{j=1}^N(b_j/\pi)^{1/4}e^{-b_jq_j^2/2}, \qquad b_j:=\sqrt{c/a_j}.$$
Each $\psi_{\mathbf n}$ belongs to $Q_{\mathrm{osc}}$, and every $u\in
Q_{\mathrm{osc}}$ satisfies the exact form expansion
$$\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\|\partial_j u\|_2^2+ c\||q|u\|_2^2 =\sum_{\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^N}\epsilon_{\mathbf n} |\langle u,\psi_{\mathbf n}\rangle|^2.$$
All parameters are positive real mathematical parameters; this lemma makes no
physical identification.

Assume Countable Choice and use $Q$, $q_h$, and the operator $h$ from
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]]. Let $\lambda_1$ be the least
eigenvalue of $h$. Then
$$\inf\{q_h(u):u\in Q,\ \|u\|_2=1\}=\lambda_1.$$
The infimum is attained by every normalized vector in the lowest eigenspace;
no simplicity or nondegeneracy is assumed.

Assume Countable Choice and the data of
[[lem-qft-polynomial-positive-compact-resolvent]]. Its variational operator $R$
is compact, self-adjoint, positive, and injective on the infinite-dimensional
complex Hilbert space $H_N$. Let $(\mu_n)_{n\ge1}$ be its positive eigenvalues
in nonincreasing order, with multiplicity, and choose corresponding
orthonormal eigenvectors $(\psi_n)_{n\ge1}$. Put
$E_n:=\mu_n^{-1}-1$ and define
$$D(S):=\left\{u=\sum_{n\ge1}c_n\psi_n\in H_N:\sum_{n\ge1}E_n^2|c_n|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad Su:=\sum_{n\ge1}E_nc_n\psi_n.$$
The series for $u$ converges in $H_N$ by the Hilbert-space expansion theorem.
Then $S$ is self-adjoint and satisfies $\langle Su,u\rangle\ge\|u\|_2^2$
for every $u\in D(S)$; also $(S+I)^{-1}=R$ is compact. For every
$u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb C)$,
$$Su=-\sum_{j=1}^Na_j\partial_j^2u+Wu.$$
Consequently $h:=S-(C_0+1)I$, on the same domain, is a self-adjoint realization
of the differential expression in
[[def-qft-regulated-polynomial-hamiltonian]] and satisfies
$\langle hu,u\rangle\ge-C_0\|u\|_2^2$ for every $u\in D(h)$.
It has compact resolvent, meaning that for some $z\in\mathbb C$ the map
$h-zI:D(h)\to H_N$ is bijective with bounded inverse on $H_N$, and that
inverse is compact; here $z=-(C_0+2)$ and $(h+(C_0+2)I)^{-1}=R$. Put
$\lambda_n:=E_n-C_0-1$, the eigenvalues of $h$; equivalently,
$$D(h)=\left\{u=\sum_nc_n\psi_n:\sum_n\lambda_n^2|c_n|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
For every $u\in Q$,
$$a(u,u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(E_n+1)|\langle u,\psi_n\rangle|^2,\qquad q_h(u):=a(u,u)-(C_0+2)\|u\|_2^2 =\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_n|\langle u,\psi_n\rangle|^2.$$
The lowest eigenvalue is attained and has finite multiplicity. This selects a
form realization; it does not assert that the differential expression on
$C_c^\infty$ is essentially self-adjoint or that it has no other self-adjoint
extensions.

derivations.claim:
Since $V_\lambda(q)=r^2q^2/2+\lambda q^4\ge (r^2/2)q^2$, the
coercivity hypotheses of [F1] and [F4] hold with $c=r^2/2$ and $C_0=0$.
Countable Choice [A1] therefore gives the form domains of [F1] and the
self-adjoint compact-resolvent form realizations with attained least
eigenvalues from [F4], for both $q_\lambda$ and $q_0$.

On $C_c^\infty$, the shifted form norms obey
$\|u\|_{Q_0}^2\le\|u\|_{Q_\lambda}^2$ because their difference is
$\lambda\int q^4|u|^2dq\ge0$. Hence the identity extends continuously
$Q_\lambda\to Q_0$, and the two continuous injections into $L^2$ identify
the same representative. On the core,
$q_\lambda(u)=q_0(u)+\lambda\int q^4|u|^2dq\ge q_0(u)$; approximating any
$u\in Q_\lambda$ by core elements and using continuity of both forms passes
this inequality to $u$. For a normalized $u$, [F3] gives
$q_0(u)\ge\epsilon_g(0)$, so taking the infimum on $Q_\lambda$ yields
$\epsilon_g(\lambda)\ge\epsilon_g(0)$.

Let $g_b(q)=(b/\pi)^{1/4}e^{-bq^2/2}$ with $b=r/\sqrt{2a}$, the
normalized ground function in [F2] for $c=r^2/2$. Choose the smooth cutoff
$\chi_R(q)=\chi(q/R)$ from [F2], with $\chi=1$ on $[-1,1]$,
$\chi=0$ outside $[-2,2]$, and $|\chi_R'|\le C/R$. Then
$u_R=\chi_Rg_b\in C_c^\infty$. For $S>R$, $u_R-u_S$ is supported where
$|q|\ge R$, and
$\|(u_R-u_S)'\|_2\le\|1_{|q|\ge R}g_b'\|_2
+C(R^{-1}+S^{-1})\|1_{|q|\ge R}g_b\|_2\to0$.
The weighted part of its $Q_\lambda$ norm is bounded in square by
$\int_{|q|\ge R}(r^2q^2/2+\lambda q^4+2)|g_b(q)|^2dq\to0$.
These tails vanish because each polynomial times $e^{-bq^2}$ is integrable:
for large $|q|$, its product with $|q|^2$ is bounded. Thus $(u_R)$ is
$Q_\lambda$-Cauchy. Its $L^2$ limit is $g_b$, so injectivity in [F1] gives
$g_b\in Q_\lambda$.

From $g_b'=-bqg_b$ and $\|g_b\|_2=1$, integrate the derivatives of
$q e^{-bq^2}$ and $q^3e^{-bq^2}$ over $\mathbb R$. Their boundary terms
vanish by Gaussian decay, giving
$\int q^2|g_b|^2dq=1/(2b)$ and
$\int q^4|g_b|^2dq=3/(4b^2)$. Hence
$q_\lambda(g_b)=ab/2+r^2/(4b)+3\lambda/(4b^2)$. At
$b=r/\sqrt{2a}$, the first two terms equal
$\epsilon_g(0)=r\sqrt{a/2}$ by [F2], and the last term is
$3a\lambda/(2r^2)$.

Since $g_b\in Q_\lambda$ is normalized, [F3] gives
$\epsilon_g(\lambda)\le q_\lambda(g_b)$. Combining this with step 2.1 and
step 3.1 yields
$0\le\epsilon_g(\lambda)-\epsilon_g(0)\le3a\lambda/(2r^2)$.

Multiplication by $E_*>0$ preserves both inequalities and gives the
stated joule-valued bound. By [A3], this is a selected-model energy
prediction and not a reported measurement.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Use one fixed finite-regulator data set from
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]], and let $h$ be the self-adjoint form
realization supplied by
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]], with domain $D(h)$ and
eigenpairs $(\psi_n,\lambda_n)$. Let $E_*>0$ joules and set
$H_{\rm phys}:=E_*h$ on $D(h)$. For physical time $\tau$ in seconds define

$$U_{\rm phys}(\tau):=U(E_*\tau/\hbar),$$

where $U(s)$ is the dimensionless-parameter group of
[[thm-qft-regulated-global-unitary-evolution]]. Then $U_{\rm phys}$ is a
strongly continuous unitary group, $U_{\rm phys}(0)=I$,
$U_{\rm phys}(\tau_1+\tau_2)=U_{\rm phys}(\tau_1)U_{\rm phys}(\tau_2)$,
and $\|U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi\|=\|\psi\|$ for every $\psi\in H_N$.
Its norm derivative exists exactly for $\psi\in D(h)$, and then

$$\frac{d}{d\tau}U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{\rm phys}U_{\rm phys}(\tau)\psi.$$

The result is a conditional deduction for the selected finite-regulator
model. It is not an empirical observation or a continuum-limit theorem.

Assume Countable Choice and use one fixed one-mode regulator with
dimensionless $a>0$, $r>0$, and $\lambda\ge0$. Here $r$ is a polynomial
coefficient, not an SI rest mass. Take
$V_\lambda(q)=\frac{r^2}{2}q^2+\lambda q^4$ on
$H_1=L^2(\mathbb R,dq;\mathbb C)$, with the form realization from
[[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]]. Let $\epsilon_g(\lambda)$
be its least eigenvalue. The physical ground-energy prediction for the
adopted scale $E_*>0$ joules is
$E_g^{\rm phys}(\lambda):=E_*\epsilon_g(\lambda)$. Then

$$0\le E_g^{\rm phys}(\lambda)-E_g^{\rm phys}(0)\le \frac{3E_*a\lambda}{2r^2}.$$

For $\lambda>0$ this is an interacting one-mode model on the full
$L^2(\mathbb R)$ space. The inequality is an exact fixed-regulator model
deduction; it supplies neither an observed energy nor a perturbation-series
or continuum-limit claim.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). A **finite-mode regulator** in this item is a fixed
finite nonempty label set $J$ with $N:=|J|\ge1$, a fixed enumeration of $J$ by
$\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and the real coordinate vector
$q=(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in\mathbb R^N$. The labels may name sites of a finite
lattice or finitely many modes; their geometry enters only through the chosen
polynomial below. No limit in $N$ is part of this definition.

Choose real coefficients $a_1,\ldots,a_N>0$, constants $c>0$ and $C_0\ge0$,
and a real polynomial $V\in\mathbb R[q_1,\ldots,q_N]$ such that
$$V(q)\ge c|q|^2-C_0\qquad(q\in\mathbb R^N).$$
Let $H_N:=L^2(\mathbb R^N,dq;\mathbb C)$, with vectors identified up to almost
everywhere equality and inner product
$$\langle u,v\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^N}u(q)\overline{v(q)}\,dq,$$
linear in the first variable. Under Countable Choice this is a complex Hilbert
space by [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Let
$D_0:=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb C)$, the smooth compactly supported
complex-valued functions. The associated **polynomial differential expression**
is the map
$$h_0:D_0\to H_N,\qquad h_0u:=-\sum_{j=1}^Na_j\partial_j^2u+Vu.$$
It is well defined because each derivative of $u$ and the product $Vu$ are
smooth and compactly supported. Set $W:=V+C_0+1$, so
$W(q)\ge1+c|q|^2$. This definition specifies finite mathematical data and a
differential expression; it does not choose a self-adjoint operator domain or
assert a continuum or infinite-volume limit.

derivations.claim:
The parameters satisfy $a>0$, $r>0$, and $\lambda>0$, and
$V(q)=q^2/2+q^4\ge q^2/2$, so the coercivity hypotheses hold with
$c=1/2$ and $C_0=0$. The coordinate remains any real $q$ in
$L^2(\mathbb R)$; the characteristic functions
$\mathbf 1_{[3n,3n+1)}$, $n\in\mathbb N$, are nonzero pairwise
orthogonal vectors, so this Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional.

By [A1], the Countable Choice hypothesis of [F2] holds. Substituting
$a=r=\lambda=1$ into it gives
$0\le E_g^{\rm phys}(1)-E_g^{\rm phys}(0)\le3E_*/2$.
This is an exact bound for the selected model, not an exact value of either
ground energy.

By [A1], the Countable Choice hypothesis of [F1] holds. Applying [F1]
to the same selected model gives a global unitary group
$U_{\rm phys}(\tau)$ for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$, norm preservation for
all states, and differentiability precisely on the stated Hamiltonian
domain. The quartic coefficient is positive, and the Hilbert space is
infinite-dimensional by step 1.1; thus this is an interacting operator model,
not a finite matrix replacement. No observation or continuum extrapolation
is asserted.
